links.targetTitle: A Facilitator rejection ends an Invocation before token hold

title: A Facilitator must give reasons for rejecting a proposal but not for approving one
content:
A.2.2.9.1.2.3.4.3 defines the Facilitator's two mutually exclusive pathways with a deliberate asymmetry in the `Commentary` field. On approval: "New value (**optional**): populate with reasoning for Approval." On rejection: "New value (**required**): populate with reasoning for Rejection." A.2.2.9.1.2.3.4.2 states the same rule in prose — "Commentary is required where the Operational Facilitator rejects the proposal for misalignment."

The asymmetry allocates the accountability burden to the decision that overrides. An approval lets the Agent's own process continue to its token holders, so it needs no defence; a rejection stops an Agent from putting its proposal to a vote, and that requires a stated ground.

Requiring written reasons also creates the material for review. A rejection with a recorded rationale can be contested, compared against other rejections, and used to build shared interpretive precedent about what counts as misalignment. An unexplained veto would leave nothing to appeal from and no way to detect inconsistency across Agents.

The cheapness of the mechanism is the point: no appeals body, no procedural burden on approvals, just a required field on the blocking branch. It is the minimum structure under which a discretionary gatekeeper can be held to a standard.
description: Commentary is explicitly optional on approval and required on rejection, so the justification burden falls only where a decision blocks an Agent's own governance.
